policies.evidencePolicy: A behavioral record is a test-runner command (swift test ..., bun test ..., vitest run ..., or mise run <task containing test>) with exit code 0 and every count > 0. For XCTest, record the 'Executed N tests, with 0 failures' line with N > 0. For swift-testing, record the 'Test run with N tests passed' line with N > 0, and only when the filter selects swift-testing tests. mise run web:check is not a behavioral record. Record bun test src and vitest run separately. An env-gated skip is never evidence. For the live agent-gateway test (LiveServedAgenticSearchTests), record only the XCTest 'Executed N' count (N > 0) of the positive run; its swift-testing 0-tests line is not counted. Tee every command into the plan's evidence directory, and give the complete log path and final exit status in each record. Session-278 logs are history only; this run's gate evidence comes from this run's logs (P1 and P3 write under their resume/ subdirectory).
policies.evidenceLayout: Evidence lives under tmp/release-0-1-17/<planId-prefix> (P1..P4), which tmp/ makes gitignored. P1 and P3 write this run's logs to tmp/release-0-1-17/<P#>/resume/. A plan never writes another plan's evidence directory.
policies.editProtocol: Follow the index 'Edit protocol': record pre/post shasum for each edit in tmp/release-0-1-17/<P#>/hashes.txt; write an immutable intent snapshot, intent.md, before the first edit; on drift, re-read, re-apply only your own intent and note the drift; edit only your own writePaths; a peer's compile or lint failure is not a blocker (rerun after the peer lands; cross-plan fixes go to P4); no git write operations; no worktrees or branches; do not create or touch .riela/; each plan updates only the Progress Log in its own plan file. Never print OPENROUTER_API_KEY or any other credential (use a presence check only), and never copy machine-local absolute paths into committed files.
policies.literalPolicy: The repository pre-commit hook rejects staged text containing absolute path literals rooted in the macOS users directory, the Linux home directory or the Nix store. No committed file written by any plan, including plan files, may contain such a literal. Use /opt/example/..., /srv/example/... or runtime-built paths. Guard regexes use character classes such as /U[s]ers/ so their own text stays clean. P4 scans the whole release diff against releaseBase.
policies.artifactPolicy: Artifact roots: tmp/release-0-1-17/<P#> for every plan, and web/dist and web/src-tauri/target for P3 and P4 (vite build output from mise run web:check and cargo output from mise run tauri:check). All are gitignored. Authored files (sources, tests, version files, README.md, plan files) are never artifact roots.
policies.protectedPaths: No plan edits any of the following: .riela/, api-key-expiration work, NoteStoreSchema or any store schema, web/src/styles.css, web/src/workspace.css, web/src/index.tsx, web/src/App.tsx, web/index.html, Sources/AppCore/AgentGatewaySubscription.swift, Sources/AppCore/ClaudeSubscriptionExecution.swift, Sources/AppServer/*, mise.toml, docker/, web/src-tauri/capabilities/, web/src-tauri/local-service/, any impl-plans/active/*-dispatch.json, signing, notarization or cask scripts, or ../homebrew-tap. design-docs/ is read-only except P2's conditional one-line AI13 'Profile additions' entry for a bounded allowance. The Step 2 design edits and these plans are committed before fanout, so P2's design-diff.log and P4's guard-design-docs.log start empty.
policies.releasePolicy: No release, tag, GitHub release, signing, notarization, cask or tap action. The operator runs .agents/skills/macos-cask-release/SKILL.md after this run.
policies.liveGatePolicy: Live agent-gateway runs need OPENROUTER_API_KEY, network access and a non-nested Seatbelt context. A missing key or a nested-sandbox 'sandbox-exec:' failure is recorded as blocked with the exact reason, never as passed. search:test-live needs Docker through colima (mise run search:docker, search:up, search:test-live, then search:down); if that is unavailable, record 'blocked: <exact error>'. tauri:check needs the gitignored local-service sidecar; if it is missing, record blocked, and do not rebuild it.
policies.escalationPolicy: P2 may add only the three AI13 bounded allowances (a global file-read-metadata, file-lock on the workspace subpath, and individual file-read* literals for non-system dylibs). designDecisionsAndRationale: Root cause per AI13: Seatbelt matches the physical path, but the profile granted the standardized (not realpath-resolved) Homebrew symlink and /etc instead of /private/etc, and it had no TLS/DNS mach services. The subscription profiles already carry the identical rules and work.
Use realpath(3) with the existing realpath+free idiom instead of URL.resolvingSymlinksInPath(), which can rewrite /private/var to /var.
Public diagnostics are an exact allowlist so that no stderr, provider text, path or secret can leak. Every unavailable error maps to one reason (DR-L1).

The sandbox-start classifier tests only the leading prefix of the whole trimmed stderr, because sandbox-exec writes before any child runs. The failing session-278 fixture echoed the prefix from a child shell under the profile, where shell startup warnings can come first. The fixture is fixed with a missing #! interpreter, so the launcher's own execvp failure produces the prefix (Step 3 observed exit 71 with this message shape).
agenticSearch moves to a new extension file, and the log sink is a defaulted stored property, to respect the 1000-line limit without an init change.

The Settings fix is two scoped light-theme rules using the background shorthand, so the result does not depend on the legacy dark cascade. The selected rule follows the primary rule at equal specificity (W16; accepted divergence DR-L2).
Waves: P1 and P2 both build in AppCore, so P2 depends on P1. P3 is web-only and runs in parallel. The Version.swift bump and the integration run come last, in P4.
intentionalTradeoffs: Duplicate /private/etc and mach-lookup rules in the subscription profiles are left as harmless duplicates.
The light theme applies unconditionally, and the legacy dark base is untouched, so dark behavior is unchanged (DR-L2).
The no-reply sandbox-start classification is a leading-prefix check on stderr; the stderr text itself is never surfaced.
